items.name: Anthropic
items.india: Bengaluru office opened 16 Feb 2026, led by Irina Ghose (ex-Microsoft India MD); hiring across applied AI, engineering, sales and management. India partnerships include Karya and the Collective Intelligence Project on locally relevant evaluations (agriculture, law).
rolesIndia: Forward Deployed Engineer (watch for India windows)

loop.note: Extremely competitive; independent research, blog posts and OSS belong at the top of the resume.
One practical OOP problem in four cumulative levels; Python strongly preferred; test-case gaming is reportedly detected.
Substantive and failable: why Anthropic specifically, what AI safety means to you, recent decisions you disagreed with.
Past systems, architectural decisions, what you would change today.
Two coding (OOP, concurrency, incremental complexity), one system design (LLM infra), one culture (45 min, every loop), one hiring manager / project.
Technical use-case screen with live Claude and an MCP scenario; customer-conversation simulation (reported as decisive); solution design for an enterprise customer.
2–4 weeks; references are taken seriously and may be requested early.

items.failsPeople: The culture/values round. Performed agreement reads as badly as dismissiveness; they want genuine engagement including disagreement.
items.aiPolicy: Draft your application yourself, then refine with Claude. Take-homes: no AI unless they say so. Live interviews: no AI unless the interviewer indicates otherwise. Prepare with Claude as much as you like.
values: Ignite a race to the top on safety
Do the simple thing that works

items.name: OpenAI
items.india: New Delhi office with Mumbai and Bengaluru planned; Prabhjeet Singh (ex-Uber India) is MD India from Sept 2026. Hiring Applied AI Engineers and Architects (Delhi, Mumbai; Technical Success org) and AI Deployment Engineers (Delhi; Startups, Bengaluru). India has 100M+ weekly ChatGPT users.
rolesIndia: AI Deployment Engineer (5+ yrs SWE/ML, Python and JavaScript, founder experience preferred)

loop.note: Background, motivation, why OpenAI, understanding of the mission.

Varies by team: pair coding, take-home project or technical test (official guide). Reported: 60-min practical screen escalating through gates; some teams a ~48-hour paid take-home work trial under NDA.
Deep probing of every decision; webhook systems, enterprise search with RBAC, rate limiters for inference, NSFW detection.
Coding, design, project presentation (often with slides), behavioral; sometimes a round with senior leadership.
Research Engineer: transformer debugging + KV cache, information theory, distributed ops. FDE: customer scenario plus LLM deployment design. Beta agentic-coding round reported on some loops.
About a week after finals; references may be requested. 3–8 weeks end to end.

items.failsPeople: Design deep-probing (name-dropping a technology you cannot defend) and incomplete multi-part coding under time; interviewers give few hints.
items.aiPolicy: Varies by track. Assume no AI unless your recruiter says otherwise; the beta agentic-coding round provides an agent and grades how you direct and verify it.
values: Ensure AGI benefits all of humanity (Charter)
Model Spec: how models should behave

items.name: Google and Google DeepMind
items.india: Large Bengaluru and Hyderabad engineering presence; ML Engineer, AI Engineer and Google Cloud AI roles post regularly. DeepMind Research Engineer roles are mostly London and Mountain View with a small Bengaluru footprint.

loop.note: Behavioral-style assessment, then a 30-minute recruiter call.
DSA in a Google Doc with no IDE; graphs and trees dominate.
1–2 coding, ML domain, ML system design, behavioral (Googleyness and leadership). Some loops are one coding round plus an AI/ML deep dive.
Feedback packet reviewed by a committee; team matching can take weeks.
Separate process: two coding rounds (code must run), gated ML 'quiz' with derivations, ML design, team-lead and culture finals; AI assistants limited in technical rounds.
Some Google loops now include reading, debugging and optimizing real code with Gemini available; graded on prompting, validation and debugging.

items.failsPeople: DeepMind ML design and the fundamentals quiz (intuition and derivations, not definitions); Googleyness is scored in every round.
items.aiPolicy: No AI in standard rounds; a separate AI-assisted format exists where Gemini is provided.
values: Googleyness: comfort with ambiguity, bias to action, collaboration

items.name: Microsoft
items.india: Hyderabad (IDC) and Bengaluru host AI engineering, Applied Scientist and Azure AI roles across CoreAI, Foundry, M365 Copilot and platform teams.

loop.note: Background, competencies, team fit; AS recruiter screens include team-specific technical questions.
~15 min ML-grounded coding (k-means, bag-of-words, top-n words), 5 min on your CV, 5–10 min fundamentals.

SWE/AI: 2–3 DSA rounds (sometimes hard), one design (AI/LLM for AI teams), behavioral woven in. AS: hiring manager + two design rounds, each half technical, half behavioral; optional extra coding round.
Prompting vs RAG vs fine-tuning, evals, production tradeoffs on the Copilot/Foundry stack.
A senior IC or manager consolidates feedback and makes the leveling call; days to weeks.

items.failsPeople: Behavioral is about half of every AS round; shallow growth-mindset answers and surface-level ML explanations get probed until gaps show.
items.aiPolicy: Some Microsoft loops use an AI-assisted coding format with approved tools; otherwise standard no-AI rounds.
values: Collaboration, drive for results, influencing for impact, judgment, adaptability

items.name: Amazon (AWS and AGI)
items.india: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi host AWS AI (Bedrock, SageMaker, Q), retail ML and Applied Science teams. As a current Amazonian, internal transfer into a Bedrock/GenAI SA or applied role is the roadmap's bridge.
rolesIndia: SDE on Bedrock / SageMaker / Q teams

loop.stage: Online assessment (SDE/MLE) or technical phone screens (AS)
loop.note: AS: 1–2 × 60 min with a senior leader, behavioral plus technical (official).
Coding (classic DSA), ML breadth, ML depth, ML system design, science application or tech talk, behavioral LPs in every round.
An interviewer from outside the team with veto power; the hardest LP probing.
Interviewers vote; the Bar Raiser must agree; team matching on level and location can be slower than the loop.
Science-style loops with heavy modern-LLM content (training techniques, perplexity and preference evals, data quality) and fewer behavioral questions.

items.failsPeople: Weak Leadership Principle stories; technically strong candidates fail on LPs. Design answers that ignore multi-tenancy, throttling and operational excellence.
items.aiPolicy: Standard no-AI rounds; a guardrailed-assistant debugging format has been described as representative.
values: Dive Deep as a technical signal
Frugality applied to GPUs: cost per token
